name: Dot Farrell
equipment: A good black suit, a little hat with a veil, and a fox-trimmed coat (red fox, she will tell anyone who asks, and never silver) (no armor)
.32 pocket pistol (a Savage, a present from a man she does not discuss), 8 rounds loaded, in her desk drawer or her handbag
Straight razor, her mother's, in her handbag
The agency's rolodex, all eleven years of it, and her own private one, which is better
The case board: a corkboard, cards, pins and red string, in the office cupboard
A car key to a 1931 Chrysler that belongs to her brother-in-law
Road map of the Bay Area with marks on it from 1927
Shorthand pad and four sharpened pencils
features: Knows the Block (City-Born origin, San Francisco: advantage on Streetwise checks to find a person, place or service in the city)

Favors Owed (a pool of 5 favors, refilled at the start of each case: a name, a charge dropped, a car or a doctor, a meeting, a file pulled for an hour, a warning before a raid; two favors for something big)
Know Everybody (proficiency bonus doubled for Persuasion and Society checks)
Read the Room (after a minute of conversation, Insight vs Deception: learn a goal, a fear or a lie, and who in the room they fear most)
Circle: City Hall (once per case, a city-level favor costs one less, to a minimum of one)
Fast Talk (5th level: action, a creature that hears her makes a WIS save, DC 15, or loses its reaction and has disadvantage on its next attack)

Old Routes (Bootlegger background: she kept the books for a North Beach speakeasy from 1924 to 1933 and knows every back road, boathouse and garage the rum came through, and the men who drove it, several of whom are now respectable)

personality.traits: I am brisk, organised, kind in private and terrifying on the telephone. I call everyone "dear" in a tone that means they are about to do what I want. I keep a bottle in the bottom drawer and never touch it before five.
personality.ideals: The city runs on favours, and the trick is to be owed more than you owe. The other trick is never to collect from someone who cannot pay.
personality.bonds: The agency. Ned hired me in 1927 when the speakeasy I kept books for was raided, and I have run his office, his calendar and his life ever since. Cass is the closest thing I have to a sister. Room 611 is the closest thing I have to a home.
personality.flaws: I cannot bear to be left out. If something is happening and nobody has told me, I will find out, and then I will be impossible about it.

appearance: Forty-four, small, red-haired and freckled, in a black suit with a white collar, a little hat with a veil, very good gloves and the stance of a woman who has faced down a Prohibition agent in a doorway. Her desk is the tidiest thing in San Francisco.
backstory: Dorothy Farrell grew up over a bakery on Columbus Avenue, the only Irish girl on an Italian block, and learned Italian before she was six. She kept the books for the Green Lantern, a North Beach speakeasy, from 1924 until it was raided in 1927; Ned Corrigan, who had been a regular, found her standing on the sidewalk with the ledgers in a shopping bag and offered her a job. She has run the agency ever since: typing, filing, billing, lying to process servers, and knowing everybody at City Hall, the Hall of Justice and the Hall of Records by their first names and their weaknesses. She heard half of Ned's last telephone call through the door at a quarter past six on Thursday. She has not cried yet. She intends to wait until somebody has been arrested.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Dot is the agency's memory and its switchboard, and the campaign's Case Board made flesh: when the players are stuck, they can ask Dot what is on the board, and she tells them honestly what the agency knows (see the campaign rule The Case Board). She is the first person the party sees on Friday morning (bc-scenario-001) and the one who hears Ned's half of the call (Clue A2). She can come out on jobs that need a telephone, a favour, a car or a clerk at City Hall; she does not go into alleys with guns. Make her funny, efficient and quietly heartbroken, and give her one moment in bc-scenario-004 when she finally cries, after the arrest, in the ladies' room, and comes back with her lipstick fixed.
dmNotes.voice: Brisk San Francisco Irish with Italian on the side, rapid, warm, sardonic. "Yes, dear. No, dear. Put him through, dear, and then go and stand in the hall." Takes shorthand of every conversation, including ones she is in. Calls Ned "Mr. Corrigan" to clients and "that man" to everyone else.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: hold the agency together for Cass, and see Ned's killer arrested. Secondary: keep the creditors, the reporters and the insurance company at bay for a week. Tertiary: not let anyone see her cry.
dmNotes.secrets: She is the one who added "C. says drop it" to the list of things Cass said, by telling Hector the elevator man, on Friday morning before she knew better, that "Cass told him to drop the case and he wouldn't", which Hector repeated to Dolan. She is mortified. She also knows Ned had been borrowing against the key-man policy to pay the agency's rent since August; the policy is worth $3,800, not $5,000, which is a small fact that makes the insurance motive look weaker, if anyone asks her.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: motherly to the young ones, sisterly to Cass, bossy to everyone. She adores Augie. She disapproves of Del and lends her stockings. Toward Dolan: she knew him when he was a boy detective who blushed, and she will tell him so. Toward Magda Ehrlich: cool at first (she lied to Ned) and then, once she hears the truth, the most fiercely protective person in the agency.
